messages.subject: Embedding knitr examples in a knitr document? (RMarkdown)
messages.subject_clean: Embedding knitr examples in a knitr document? (RMarkdown)
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I was wondering if anyone know of a good way to embed knitr code examples within a knitr document such that the final .md file will include the raw knitr commands?

For example, I would like the final .md file to include something like:

    ```{r}
    print('Hello World')
    ```

Currently, however, the knitr commands are always parsed and the curly braces are removed.

I tried escaping the opening curly brace with a backslash, and that prevents the code from executing, but the backslash stays in the final document. I also tried including the HTML escape code for the opening brace, but the santization in knitr then escapes the '&' in the entity code so that output does not show the curly brace.

It would be great if there is a way to achieve the above effect such that the knitr code examples themselves also have the usual syntax highlighting applied to R code blocks, but even just an anonymous (indented) Markdown code block would be sufficient.

Any ideas?

Thanks,
Keith

```{r,fig.height=2,fig.width=2}
plot(phy,no.margin=TRUE)
```

messages.subject: figures: separating code (inline) and figure(s) (float)
messages.subject_clean: figures: separating code (inline) and figure(s) (float)
messages.body_plain:
I'm revising a legacy Sweave vignette to use knitr, after running Sweave2knitr() on the .Rnw file.

Under Sweave, in order to have the text and code for a figure appear inline, but the generated figures appear in a
float, I resorted to doing things manually, e.g., generating the figure in a chunk, then writing an explicit
\begin{figure} ... \end{figure} using \includegraphics{}.  Otherwise, if I included the chunk within the
figure environment, the code would appear in the float.

Is there some way to clean this up in knitr?  i.e., use knitr features to achieve this?
One problem is that I often have long figure captions,
and knitr requires that the <<*>>= stuff be all on one line.

An earlier post by Frank Harrell seemed to imply that he had created some customizations for these
purposes, but that is fairly old
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/knitr/includegraphics|sort:date/knitr/bYj3Zn11hjE/1SYK9k8iv7sJ <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/knitr/includegraphics%7Csort:date/knitr/bYj3Zn11hjE/1SYK9k8iv7sJ>

Here is an excerpt from the file:

<<include=FALSE>>=
opts_chunk$set(engine='R',fig.height=6,fig.width=7,results='hide',fig.show='hide',echo=TRUE)
opts_chunk$set(fig.path='fig/vcd-tut-')
opts_chunk$set(tidy=FALSE)
@

...

The resulting \code{ca} object can be plotted just by running the \codefun{plot}
method on the \code{ca} object, giving the result in
\figref{fig:ca-haireye}.  \codefun{plot.ca <http://plot.ca>} does not allow labels for dimensions;
these can be added with \codefun{title}.
It can be seen that most of the association is accounted for by the ordering
of both hair color and eye color along Dimension 1, a dark to light dimension.
<<ca-haireye,echo=TRUE,fig.keep='high'>>=
plot(ca(HairEye), main="Hair Color and Eye Color")
title(xlab="Dim 1 (89.4%)", ylab="Dim 2 (9.5%)")
@

\begin{figure}[htb]
\begin{center}
%<<ca-haireye,results='hide',echo=FALSE>>=
%plot(ca(HairEye), main="Hair Color and Eye Color")
%title(xlab="Dim 1 (89.4%)", ylab="Dim 2 (9.5%)")
%@
\includegraphics[width=0.7\textwidth]{fig/vcd-tut-ca-haireye}
\caption{Correspondence analysis plot for the \data{HairEye} data.}
\label{fig:ca-haireye}
\end{center}
\end{figure}

there since knitr v0.9 (Jan 2013), although I did not promote it
particularly. See example 103 at
https://github.com/yihui/knitr-examples

do that and manually \includegraphics{} later, because you have to
worry about figure filenames, e.g. when you change the chunk label,
you will have to manually update the filename accordingly.

I agree that it is cumbersome to write a long caption (fig.cap="....")
in a chunk header in one line, and that is one motivation for the
document hook hook_movecode(). Other chunk options should be short and
easy to write, e.g. fig.align="center" (so that you do not have to
\begin{center}\end{center})

Since I have finished the knitr book in LaTeX, I'm relatively
confident that most LaTeX headache/problems that you can think of have
probably been solved. Maybe I should start writing checks of $2.56 for

As you said, that is caused by the alltt and verbatim environments for
the source code and output, respectively. Both environments add
vertical space around them by default. I just googled a while, and
found one solution for verbatim but not alltt:

http://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/43331/control-vertical-space-before-and-after-verbatim-environment

This solution alone won't work. I do not know how to remove the
vertical space for alltt. You may try StackExchange.

If you do not mind syntax highlighting, you can turn off the highlight
option, e.g.

<<highlight=FALSE>>=

  A <- matrix(1:4, nrow=2)
  A
@

Then everything will be in a single verbatim environment, and you will
no longer have the space problem.

messages.body_plain:
This bug is actually more general than I thought.  In my example, it was triggered by the \texttt{1:10}
in fig1, and thus all fig.cap containing some Latex code are prone to this error in the
composing of the fig.scap.

The work-around for now is to use fig.scap='' whenever you use Latex code withing a fig.cap.
The following now works:

% !Rnw weave = knitr
\documentclass{article}

<<knitr-setup, include=FALSE>>=
options(width=70)
opts_chunk$set(fig.align='center', fig.height=6, fig.width=7, fig.pos='hbt!')
opts_chunk$set(out.width = '.6\\linewidth')

@

\begin{document}
Testing fig ref in a fig caption...

Plot one figure...

<<fig1, fig.cap='Plot of \\texttt{1:10}', fig.scap=''>>=

plot(1:10)
@
Then, refer to it in another...

<<fig2, fig.cap='The same plot shown in Figure \\ref{fig:fig1}', fig.scap=''>>=
plot(1:10)
@
\end{document}
